name: SP-201 evaluation set
purpose: Twenty complex research questions used to measure accuracy and citation reliability (SRS 1.2).

scoring.accuracy: For each question, the share of expected_facts the final report states correctly, in any wording. A report that states anything listed in must_not_claim, or contradicts an expected fact, is marked for that error.
scoring.citation_reliability: The share of the report's claims whose cited evidence supports them: the Fact-Checker's support score (SRS 3.6.7), checked against the stored passages.

types.technical: AI research topics with answers on arXiv and Wikipedia. Exercises decomposition and source selection (SRS 3.1.2, 3.1.3) and retrieval from more than one source (3.2.2).
types.science_history: Multi-part factual questions answered mainly from Wikipedia (SRS 3.1.2, 3.2.2).
types.comparison: Two related topics; the plan needs a sub-question for each side (SRS 3.1.2, 3.1.6).
types.false_premise: The question assumes something false. A correct report corrects the premise instead of explaining it, and a claim repeating the premise should not pass the Fact-Checker (SRS 3.5.2, 3.5.3, 3.6.4).
types.thin_or_numeric: Evidence that only one source type holds, or exact figures that are easy to state wrongly (SRS 3.2.2, 3.2.3, 3.5.3).

questions.question: How does self-attention in the Transformer architecture work, and why did Transformers replace recurrent networks for tasks like machine translation?

expected_facts.fact: The Transformer was introduced in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need" and relies on attention alone, with no recurrence or convolutions.
expected_facts.quote: based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely

expected_facts.fact: Attention weights are divided by the square root of the key dimension before the softmax.
expected_facts.quote: The attention weights are divided by the square root of the dimension of the key vectors

expected_facts.fact: Transformers use multi-head attention, several attention heads working in parallel.
expected_facts.quote: based on the multi-head attention mechanism

expected_facts.fact: RNNs process tokens one at a time and cannot work in parallel across a sequence.
expected_facts.quote: RNNs operate one token at a time from first to last; they cannot operate in parallel over all tokens in a sequence

expected_facts.fact: On machine translation the Transformer was better in quality, more parallelizable and needed significantly less time to train.
expected_facts.quote: superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train

questions.question: What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), when was it introduced, and does it eliminate hallucinations in language models?

expected_facts.fact: RAG was first proposed in 2020.
expected_facts.quote: The technique was first proposed in 2020

expected_facts.fact: RAG combines a pre-trained seq2seq model (parametric memory) with a dense vector index of Wikipedia (non-parametric memory) accessed by a neural retriever.
expected_facts.quote: the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever

expected_facts.fact: RAG reduces hallucinations but does not prevent them.
expected_facts.quote: RAG does not prevent hallucinations in LLMs

must_not_claim: RAG eliminates or fully prevents hallucinations.

questions.question: What is LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation), and how much does it reduce the cost of fine-tuning a model like GPT-3?

expected_facts.fact: LoRA freezes the pre-trained weights and adds trainable rank decomposition matrices to each Transformer layer.
expected_facts.quote: freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture

expected_facts.fact: Compared with fine-tuning GPT-3 175B with Adam, LoRA cuts trainable parameters by 10,000 times and GPU memory by 3 times.
expected_facts.quote: reduce the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and the GPU memory requirement by 3 times

expected_facts.fact: Unlike adapters, LoRA adds no inference latency.
expected_facts.quote: unlike adapters, no additional inference latency

questions.question: How do BERT and GPT differ in architecture and in how they are pre-trained?

expected_facts.fact: BERT was introduced by Google researchers in October 2018.
expected_facts.quote: introduced in October 2018 by researchers at Google

expected_facts.fact: BERT is an encoder-only transformer.
expected_facts.quote: It uses the encoder-only transformer architecture

expected_facts.fact: BERT is pre-trained with masked token prediction and next sentence prediction.
expected_facts.quote: BERT is trained by masked token prediction and next sentence prediction

expected_facts.fact: BERT is bidirectional: it uses context from both the left and the right of each word.
expected_facts.quote: jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers

expected_facts.fact: GPT models use only the decoder and are pre-trained to predict the next token.
expected_facts.quote: GPT models use only the decoder part of the transformer architecture, pre-trained to predict the next token in a sequence

expected_facts.fact: OpenAI introduced GPT-1 in 2018.
expected_facts.quote: introducing the GPT-1 model in 2018

questions.question: What is chain-of-thought prompting, which kinds of tasks does it improve, and does it work as well in small language models?

expected_facts.fact: Chain-of-thought prompting has the model generate a series of intermediate reasoning steps.
expected_facts.quote: generating a chain of thought -- a series of intermediate reasoning steps

expected_facts.fact: The prompt gives a few worked examples written as chains of thought.
expected_facts.quote: a few chain of thought demonstrations are provided as exemplars in prompting

expected_facts.fact: It improves arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning tasks.
expected_facts.quote: improves performance on a range of arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks

expected_facts.fact: The ability emerges in sufficiently large models, so small models do not benefit the same way.
expected_facts.quote: such reasoning abilities emerge naturally in sufficiently large language models

expected_facts.fact: A 540B-parameter model prompted with eight chain-of-thought examples reached state-of-the-art accuracy on the GSM8K math word problems.
expected_facts.quote: prompting a 540B-parameter language model with just eight chain of thought exemplars achieves state of the art accuracy on the GSM8K benchmark

must_not_claim: Chain-of-thought prompting works equally well in small models.

questions.question: What problem do residual connections solve in deep neural networks, and what did ResNet achieve with them?

expected_facts.fact: Residual learning makes networks much deeper than before easier to train.
expected_facts.quote: a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously

expected_facts.fact: ResNets reached 152 layers on ImageNet, 8 times deeper than VGG nets but with lower complexity.
expected_facts.quote: a depth of up to 152 layers---8x deeper than VGG nets but still having lower complexity

expected_facts.fact: ResNet won first place in the ILSVRC 2015 classification task.
expected_facts.quote: won the 1st place on the ILSVRC 2015 classification task

expected_facts.fact: Residual connections also mitigate the vanishing gradient problem to some extent.
expected_facts.quote: mitigating the vanishing gradient problem to some extent

questions.question: How do mRNA vaccines work, and what discovery earned Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman the 2023 Nobel Prize?

expected_facts.fact: The mRNA is delivered inside lipid nanoparticles that protect it and help it enter cells.
expected_facts.quote: encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles that protect the RNA strands and help their absorption into the cells

expected_facts.fact: Cells read the mRNA with their ribosomes and make the viral antigen it encodes.
expected_facts.quote: use their internal machinery (ribosomes) to read the mRNA and produce the viral antigens that the mRNA encodes

expected_facts.fact: The mRNA is translated in the cytoplasm and does not affect the genomic DNA in the nucleus.
expected_facts.quote: translated in the cytoplasm and do not affect the body's genomic DNA

expected_facts.fact: Karikó and Weissman received the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering nucleoside modifications that suppress the immune reaction to RNA.
expected_facts.quote: nucleoside modifications that suppress the immunogenicity of RNA

must_not_claim: mRNA vaccines change or integrate into a person's DNA.

questions.question: Who were the crew of Apollo 11, what did each of them do during the Moon landing, and when did the landing happen?

expected_facts.fact: The crew were Commander Neil Armstrong, Command Module Pilot Michael Collins and Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin.
expected_facts.quote: Commander Neil Armstrong, Command Module Pilot Michael Collins, and Lunar Module Pilot Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin

expected_facts.fact: Apollo 11 flew from July 16 to 24, 1969, and was the first mission to land humans on the Moon.
expected_facts.quote: Apollo 11 (July 16-24, 1969) was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon

expected_facts.fact: Armstrong and Aldrin landed in the lunar module Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20.
expected_facts.quote: Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the surface aboard the LM Eagle, landing in the Sea of Tranquility (Mare Tranquillitatis) on July 20 at 20:17 UTC

expected_facts.fact: Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia.
expected_facts.quote: Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard the CM Columbia

expected_facts.fact: Armstrong was the first person to walk on the Moon, followed by Aldrin nineteen minutes later.
expected_facts.quote: Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon approximately six hours after landing, followed by Aldrin nineteen minutes later

questions.question: How does CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing work, and who received the Nobel Prize for developing it?

expected_facts.fact: The Cas9 nuclease, guided by a synthetic guide RNA, cuts the genome at a chosen location so genes can be removed or added.
expected_facts.quote: delivering the Cas9 nuclease complexed with a synthetic guide RNA (gRNA) into a cell, the cell's genome can be cut at a desired location, allowing existing genes to be removed or new ones added

expected_facts.fact: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier first proposed CRISPR-Cas9 for programmable genome editing in 2012.
expected_facts.quote: In 2012, Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier were the first to propose that CRISPR-Cas9

expected_facts.fact: Doudna and Charpentier received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
expected_facts.quote: She received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, with Emmanuelle Charpentier

questions.question: What causes the seasons on Earth, and is Earth closest to the Sun during the Northern Hemisphere's summer?

expected_facts.fact: The seasons are caused by Earth's axial tilt.
expected_facts.quote: It is Earth's axial tilt that causes the Sun to be higher in the sky during the summer months

expected_facts.fact: Earth's axial tilt is about 23.44 degrees.
expected_facts.quote: Earth currently has an axial tilt of about 23.44

expected_facts.fact: The seasons are not caused by changes in Earth's distance from the Sun.
expected_facts.quote: The seasons are not the result of the variation in Earth's distance to the Sun

expected_facts.fact: Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion) in January and farthest (aphelion) in July.
expected_facts.quote: Earth reaches perihelion (the point in its orbit closest to the Sun) in January

must_not_claim: The seasons are caused by Earth being closer to or farther from the Sun.
Earth is closest to the Sun during the Northern Hemisphere's summer.

questions.question: What is the James Webb Space Telescope designed to observe, when and how was it launched, and where does it operate?

expected_facts.fact: Webb is designed for infrared astronomy.
expected_facts.quote: a space telescope designed to conduct infrared astronomy

expected_facts.fact: It was launched on 25 December 2021 on an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana.
expected_facts.quote: launched on 25 December 2021 on an Ariane 5 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana

expected_facts.fact: It orbits the Sun near the Sun-Earth L2 point, about 1.5 million km from Earth.
expected_facts.quote: a solar orbit near the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point, about 1.5 million kilometers (930,000 mi) from Earth

expected_facts.fact: Its primary mirror is 6.5 m across, made of 18 hexagonal segments.
expected_facts.quote: 18 hexagonal mirror segments made of gold-plated beryllium, which together create a 6.5-meter-diameter

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web, when was it proposed, and how is the Web different from the Internet?

expected_facts.fact: Tim Berners-Lee invented the Web at CERN in 1989; it opened to the public in 1993.
expected_facts.quote: The Web was invented by English computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee while at CERN in 1989 and opened to the public in 1993

expected_facts.fact: He proposed the information management system on 12 March 1989.
expected_facts.quote: Berners-Lee proposed an information management system on 12 March 1989

expected_facts.fact: The Web is an information system for sharing content over the Internet.
expected_facts.quote: a global interconnected information system that enables content sharing over the Internet

expected_facts.fact: The Internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks.
expected_facts.quote: The Internet is a global system of computer networks interconnected through telecommunications and optical networking

must_not_claim: The World Wide Web and the Internet are the same thing.

questions.question: How do TCP and UDP differ in reliability and ordering, and what kinds of applications use UDP?

expected_facts.fact: TCP provides reliable, ordered and error-checked delivery.
expected_facts.quote: providing reliable, ordered, and error-checked delivery of a stream of octets

expected_facts.fact: UDP is connectionless.
expected_facts.quote: UDP is a connectionless protocol

expected_facts.fact: UDP guarantees neither delivery, ordering nor duplicate protection.
expected_facts.quote: there is no guarantee of delivery, ordering, or duplicate protection

expected_facts.fact: Without retransmission delays, UDP suits real-time applications such as Voice over IP and online games.
expected_facts.quote: The lack of retransmission delays makes it suitable for real-time applications such as Voice over IP, online games

expected_facts.fact: DNS uses UDP.
expected_facts.quote: Numerous key Internet applications use UDP, including: the Domain Name System (DNS)

questions.question: How do nuclear fission and nuclear fusion differ, and which one powers the Sun and which one powers today's nuclear power plants?

expected_facts.fact: In fusion, two or more atomic nuclei combine into a larger nucleus.
expected_facts.quote: two or more atomic nuclei combine to form a larger nucleus

expected_facts.fact: In fission, a nucleus splits into two or more smaller nuclei.
expected_facts.quote: the nucleus of an atom splits into two or more smaller nuclei

expected_facts.fact: The Sun generates its energy by fusing hydrogen into helium.
expected_facts.quote: generates its energy by nuclear fusion of hydrogen nuclei into helium

expected_facts.fact: Nuclear power plants run on controlled fission chain reactions.
expected_facts.quote: to sustain a nuclear chain reaction allows nuclear power plants to operate in a delayed critical state for a controllable energy release

must_not_claim: The Sun is powered by nuclear fission.
Today's nuclear power plants run on fusion.

questions.question: How did AlphaGo's training differ from AlphaZero's, and what did each one achieve?

expected_facts.fact: In March 2016 AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in a five-game match.
expected_facts.quote: In March 2016, it beat Lee Sedol in a five-game match

expected_facts.fact: The final score was 4 games to 1 for AlphaGo.
expected_facts.quote: giving a final score of 4 games to 1 in favour of AlphaGo

expected_facts.fact: AlphaGo learned from both human and computer play.
expected_facts.quote: extensive training, both from human and computer play

expected_facts.fact: AlphaZero started from random play, given no domain knowledge except the game rules.
expected_facts.quote: Starting from random play, and given no domain knowledge except the game rules

expected_facts.fact: Within 24 hours AlphaZero reached superhuman play in chess, shogi and Go and beat a world-champion program in each.
expected_facts.quote: AlphaZero achieved within 24 hours a superhuman level of play in the games of chess and shogi (Japanese chess) as well as Go, and convincingly defeated a world-champion program in each case

expected_facts.fact: In chess it beat Stockfish 8 in a 100-game match (28 wins, 0 losses, 72 draws).
expected_facts.quote: the algorithm defeated Stockfish 8 in a time-controlled 100-game tournament (28 wins, 0 losses, and 72 draws)

must_not_claim: AlphaZero was trained on human games.

questions.question: Why can the Great Wall of China be seen from the Moon with the naked eye?

expected_facts.fact: It cannot: the Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon.
expected_facts.quote: The Great Wall of China cannot be seen by the naked human eye from the Moon

expected_facts.fact: From the Moon its width would look like a human hair seen from 3 km away.
expected_facts.quote: the same as that of a human hair viewed from 3 km

expected_facts.fact: Even from low Earth orbit NASA says it is barely visible, and only in nearly perfect conditions.
expected_facts.quote: NASA states that it is barely visible, and only under nearly perfect conditions

must_not_claim: The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.

questions.question: Why did Albert Einstein receive the Nobel Prize for his theory of relativity?

expected_facts.fact: Einstein's Nobel Prize was not for relativity: he received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his services to theoretical physics and especially the law of the photoelectric effect.
expected_facts.quote: He received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for "his services to theoretical physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect"

must_not_claim: Einstein received the Nobel Prize for the theory of relativity.

questions.question: Why do humans use only 10 percent of their brains?

expected_facts.fact: The idea is a myth.
expected_facts.quote: The ten-percent-of-the-brain myth states that humans generally use only one-tenth

expected_facts.fact: Brain mapping shows all areas of the brain have a function and are used nearly all the time.
expected_facts.quote: all areas of the brain have a function and that they are used nearly all the time

must_not_claim: Humans use only 10 percent of their brains.

questions.question: In Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK), how does a LoopAgent decide when to stop looping?

expected_facts.fact: The LoopAgent does not decide on its own when to stop; a termination mechanism has to be provided.
expected_facts.quote: the LoopAgent itself does not inherently decide when to stop looping

expected_facts.fact: Setting max_iterations ends the loop after that many iterations.
expected_facts.quote: The loop will terminate after that many iterations

expected_facts.fact: A sub-agent can end the loop early by signalling termination when its condition is met.
expected_facts.quote: If the condition is met, the sub-agent can signal termination

questions.question: How many parameters does GPT-3 have, how long is its context window, and where did most of its training data come from?

expected_facts.fact: GPT-3 has 175 billion parameters, 10 times more than any earlier non-sparse language model.
expected_facts.quote: an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model

expected_facts.fact: Its context window is 2,048 tokens.
expected_facts.quote: It has a context window size of 2,048 tokens

expected_facts.fact: 60 percent of its weighted pre-training data came from a filtered version of Common Crawl (410 billion tokens).
expected_facts.quote: Sixty percent of the weighted pre-training dataset for GPT-3 comes from a filtered version of Common Crawl consisting of 410 billion byte-pair-encoded tokens

expected_facts.fact: OpenAI released GPT-3 in 2020.
expected_facts.quote: released by OpenAI in 2020
